design_decision: The distinction is carried by which graded fail_check value the open-row/rc==0 branch returns, not by a new exit code or a new vocabulary entry. When the row never closed (status != done) and the worker exited 0, the branch now asks proof-of-work FIRST: work_present = bool(deliverables) and not dl_missing (every declared deliverable exists on disk). If work_present and the nonce was NOT echoed, the outcome is a PROTOCOL failure — fail=nonce (RECOVERABLE per model-profiles.py), with a summary that says WORK PRESENT explicitly and a NOTE detail line naming the reclassification, so the distinction is visible in both the graded datum and the prose. If work is absent (no deliverables declared, or any declared one missing) the branch is untouched: fail=row (UNRECOVERABLE), exactly as before — this is the genuine kimi-incident shape the arm exists to catch, and it must not soften. The one case the design leaves alone: work_present is True AND the nonce WAS echoed but the row still never closed (the worker did everything except call `managent done`). No RECOVERABLE_FAIL value fits 'work done, protocol followed, row just never closed', and model-profiles.py is out of scope for this patch (deliverables=tools/dispatch_verify.py only), so that near-impossible residual state keeps falling through to fail=row unchanged.

behaviour (not covered by any existing arm): the T818 shape — task in in_progress, rc=0, every declared deliverable present on disk, nonce not echoed — changes from (fail_check=row, summary 'task never left in_progress') to (fail_check=nonce, summary names 'WORK PRESENT ... protocol failure, not absence of work'), reproduced directly against both the patched and unpatched module in a scratch harness
concerns: The one state this patch does not resolve: work_present True AND nonce_ok True with the row still open (worker did the work, echoed the token, but never called `managent done`). No RECOVERABLE_FAIL bucket fits 'protocol mostly followed, close step missing', and extending that vocabulary is model-profiles.py's territory, out of this patch's scope (a patch touching anything but tools/dispatch_verify.py is disqualified). It keeps falling through to fail=row, silently indistinguishable from true absence of work — a narrower but real residue of the same defect class.

work_present is computed from the SAME deliverables/dl_missing pass that already ran above this branch (lines 961-970) — it does not re-stat the filesystem or add a second existence check, but it also does not re-validate findings-deliverable parsing (findings_bad) for this branch: a findings deliverable that exists on disk but fails to parse still counts as work_present here. That combination (open row + malformed findings + missing nonce) is untested and unclassified by this patch; T818 itself was not this shape (its manifest and findings all parsed), so I judged it out of the race's stated scope.

The rc!=0 open-row path (lines 1023-1033) is completely untouched: a worker that crashes or is killed after producing every deliverable still reports fail=row via the unreached/directive_kill/plain-exit branches below this one. The race brief's incident (T818) was specifically the rc==0 case; I did not extend the same proof-of-work check to rc!=0 because none of the 172 arms exercise that combination and I could not verify a rc!=0+work-present shape against a real incident the way T818 anchors the rc==0 one.
